sections.html:
Anything that changes or burdens Clay County land lands on the Recorder of Deeds' desk: deeds, deeds of trust, plats, surveys, powers of attorney and tax liens. Walk-ins go to the Administration building, 1 Courthouse Square, Liberty. Mail is addressed to PO Box 238, Liberty, MO 64069. The phone is 816-407-3550 and the email is recorder@claycountymo.gov.

Doors stay open until 5:00 p.m. on weekdays, yet recording and marriage licenses stop at 4:00 p.m. A deed signed late in the day must reach the counter before that hour, so ask the title company who is delivering it and how. The Annex does not have a recorder window. Everything goes to the courthouse square.

A short checklist before you go: the original signed deed with a notary acknowledgment, the full legal description, the grantee's mailing address, and a check for the right amount. Missing any one of these is the usual reason for a rejection and a lost day.

Staff do not decide what should be recorded. They check a document against state requirements and then keep it forever as a public record.

A standard document costs $26.00 on its first page, then $3.00 for every page that follows. Pay with cash, a check or a credit card, which brings a separate processor fee. A statewide change on August 28, 2026 added a flat $2.00 to recording charges, so a fee sheet saved before then understates the cost.

A military discharge is recorded for nothing. State law adds its own piece: RSMo 59.319 puts a six dollar user fee on each recorded instrument, and half of that stays with the recorder to pay for storing and preserving records. Because a long document is priced by the page, call ahead with your page count.

sections.h2: Format rules that can get a deed refused
sections.html:
Under RSMo 59.310 the recorder may turn away a document that ignores the format rules, or accept it as non-standard for $25.00 more. The county posts the full standards on its document standards page.

  • Plain letter-size paper in white or a light color, 20 pound weight, no watermark or logo, printed on one side only.
  • Use dark ink and type no smaller than 8 point, and place a typed, stamped or printed name below each signature.
  • Reserve a blank three-inch strip at the top of page one, and leave three quarters of an inch elsewhere.
  • The first page needs the title, date, each grantor and marital status, each grantee, statutory addresses, the legal description and any book and page reference.

Use the complete legal description, and do not copy it off a tax bill. The rules do not apply to documents signed before January 1, 2002, military separation papers, papers executed abroad, certified copies and court judgments. If the office rejects a document, it returns it with the reason in writing.

sections.h2: How to find or copy a recorded deed
sections.html:
Go to claymo.icounty.com for the online index. A free registration lets you view document images, but copies cost money. Subscription problems go to iCounty at (816) 295-1540, and every other question goes to the recorder at 816-407-3550.

The index is by name, which makes a street-address search useless. A printout from the Assessor's real estate division lists the deed's book and page and makes a copy request quicker. The online collection covers 1968 forward. Before an automated database began in 1986, deeds were copied by hand into books going back to 1822, and daily imaging began in August 1999.

A copy costs $2.00 for the first page and $1.00 for each later one, and certifying a document adds $1.00. If you pay by card, the copies can be emailed or mailed.

sections.h2: What the recorder will not do
sections.html:
By statute the office cannot look for liens or say whether any exist. Search yourself at the public computer or pay a title company to do it. Recorded deeds are also fixed. To add or drop a name you need a new deed, drawn up and filed at the current rate.

  • Sale prices: not part of the record here, though the Assessor may share the area's market value.
  • Building details: recorded files describe land, so ask the Assessor when improvements went up.
  • Blank forms: staff may not draft legal papers, so a quit claim or warranty deed must come from you or an attorney.
  • Foreclosure lists: look for notices in the Kearney Courier or the Excelsior Springs Daily Standard and call the named trustee.

When a mortgage is paid off, a release of the deed of trust gets recorded. That release does not prove you own the house. The deed from your seller does. Deed Watch, a free email alert at deedwatch.com, will message you whenever a document is recorded under a name you pick.

Greater Kansas City covers this county, including the northern suburbs and a piece of the city itself. An estimated 265,032 people and 110,443 housing units were here in July 2025. Of those homes, 69.5% have owners living in them. The median value of an owner-occupied home came to $275,600 in 2020 to 2024, household income to $88,468 and rent to $1,243. Builders took out 297 permits in 2025.

A house in Liberty, Gladstone, Kearney, Smithville or North Kansas City is filed at the same Liberty counter. Confirm with the closing attorney or title company who will carry the deed over, so it gets there before 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: What does filing a deed cost?
faqs.a: Page one is $26.00 and every further page $3.00, plus $25.00 if the document is non-standard. The flat $2.00 statewide increase from August 28, 2026 is already built in. Call 816-407-3550 to check page counts and card fees.

faqs.q: Until what time can a deed be filed?
faqs.a: 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, even though the building stays open until 5:00 p.m. The counter is at 1 Courthouse Square in Liberty, and mail goes to PO Box 238.

faqs.q: Can I search a deed by street address?
faqs.a: No, the index is by name. Ask the Assessor's real estate division for the book and page, then use the online search or phone the office. Viewing online is free after registration, and copies are paid.

faqs.q: Can the recorder fix a name or legal description on a deed that is already recorded?
faqs.a: No, a recorded document is permanent and cannot be edited. Fixing the title takes a new deed or corrective document, prepared by you or an attorney and recorded for the current fee.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax line on the fee schedule?
faqs.a: None appears. The schedule covers recording, copies, certification, plats, liens and marriage licenses. For any other closing cost, ask the Recorder at 816-407-3550 or your title company.
